problem: Prior navigation systems depend on pre-built HD maps, manually specified point goals, or short-horizon indoor settings, so they cannot turn abstract human requests (e.g. 'I want to go for a walk') into long-horizon, socially compliant outdoor navigation with explicit safety reasoning at crossings and crowds.
motivation: Human-centric applications such as last-mile delivery and blind guidance need robots to infer real-world destinations from abstract intent and accompany users safely over kilometer-scale outdoor routes. The key observation is that the global grounding and coarse route information needed is already available from public map services (GPS, POIs, walking-route APIs), so no HD map is needed.
key_idea: Decouple where to go from how to walk there: a high-level VLM grounds the instruction to a public-map POI, builds a coarse waypoint route, and jointly routes and safety-checks each step, while a low-level VLA generates socially compliant local trajectories.
insight: Both the high-level VLM and the low-level policy matter in real-world success, and the low-level policy matters more. In the ablation on the two delivery scenarios, VLM choice ranged 30-60% SR (MiMo-Embodied best), while VLA choice ranged 20% (GNM/ViNT) to 60% (SocialNav), so a socially aware local policy helps turns, detours and pedestrian proximity. Failures concentrate in ambiguous crossings and crowds, so fine-grained VLM safety reasoning remains the bottleneck.
method: POI-aware destination grounding: the high-level VLM proposes place categories from the instruction, these are queried against a public map service (Baidu/Google/Gaode) around the user's GPS, and the VLM picks one destination from the candidate set with a rationale.

Route retrieval and waypoint construction: the walking-route API path is simplified into an ordered geo-referenced waypoint sequence that keeps crossing and traffic-light cues, then aligned to the robot's local frame.

Joint routing and safety decision: at each step the high-level VLM sees the RGB image, a step-aware route instruction and the lookahead waypoint, and outputs (routine/complex, proceed/stop-and-wait, confidence, reason).
Low-level VLA: takes the egocentric image, route instruction, local goal and recent pose history, and predicts a short-horizon trajectory that is re-planned every step.

Stop-and-wait safety execution: the robot proceeds only if the decision is proceed and confidence ≥ α; otherwise it stays put, re-observes and re-queries within a limited budget, and hands control back to the operator if the budget runs out.

Closed-loop execution: the VLA trajectory is fused with the SLAM pose into a target pose for the AGV controller, after a short in-place yaw alignment. Arrival tolerance and a hard iteration budget end the episode.

setting.backbone: High-level: frozen VLM (MiMo-Embodied best in ablation; also Claude-Sonnet, Gemini-3-Flash, GPT-5, Qwen3-VL-8B, RoboBrain 2.0). Low-level: SocialNav VLA (reproduced) as the best policy.
setting.training_data: Not specified. VLMs are used off-the-shelf, and the low-level VLAs are reproduced implementations (SocialNav, CityWalker, GNM, ViNT, NoMaD) with no new training described.
setting.observation: Forward RGB (RealSense D455 RGB-D, only RGB used) + GPS + SLAM pose and pose history
setting.action_space: Predicted short-horizon local trajectory converted to target poses for the AGV controller; zero-displacement stop action
setting.privileged: none (uses public map services for POIs and walking routes as a prior)

numbers.backbone: High-level VLM (variant unspecified in main experiment) + SocialNav low-level VLA
numbers.extra: Athena 2.0 Pro AGV; remote H20 inference server; public map service

numbers.eval_set_note: Last-mile delivery only (2 scenarios x 5 trials = 10 trials)
numbers.extra: Milk tea to Building B 4/5 (80%); package to Building A 3/5 (60%)
numbers.evidence: The last-mile delivery category achieves 70% task-level SR over 10 trials

numbers.eval_set_note: Blind guidance only (2 scenarios x 5 trials = 10 trials)
numbers.extra: Go for a walk 3/5 (60%); go shopping 2/5 (40%)

numbers.method: Walk with Me w/ MiMo-Embodied high-level VLM
numbers.extra: Low-level VLA fixed; best VLM in ablation

numbers_note: Only real-world trial counts are reported (20 trials total, no baselines in main experiment). Ablation rows: VLMs Claude-Sonnet 50, Gemini-3-Flash 40, GPT-5 50, Qwen3-VL-8B 30, RoboBrain 2.0 50; VLAs GNM 20, ViNT 20, NoMaD 30, CityWalker 50, SocialNav 60 (all SR%, 10 trials).
results: The complete system succeeds in 12/20 real-world outdoor trials (60% SR): 70% for last-mile delivery and 50% for blind guidance. In ablations on delivery, the best high-level VLM (MiMo-Embodied) reaches 60%, and the best low-level policy (SocialNav) reaches 60% versus 20% for GNM/ViNT and 50% for CityWalker.
limitations: Small-scale real-world evaluation (20 trials, 10 per ablation), with no comparison against end-to-end baselines and no statistical significance.
Depends on public map service accuracy, GPS/localization noise, and VLM/VLA robustness in rare or ambiguous dynamic scenes. VLM safety responses diverge under ambiguous observations.
Relies on remote GPU inference and API calls, and aborts to the operator when no confident proceed decision is reached.
